authority.summary: Drupal's Internal Page Cache documentation describes what the maximum-age value controls, and names the deployment contexts in which disabling page caching is deliberate rather than a defect.

context_requirements.subject: deployment
context_requirements.why_it_matters: The documentation states a site behind a reverse caching proxy or CDN can disable page caching safely. Drupal Knowledge observes no deployment topology, so whether this value is deliberate here is unknown.

finding.assertion: Exported configuration sets the browser and proxy cache maximum age to 0.

conclusion.candidate: Browsers and proxies are told not to cache pages, and the deployment context that would decide whether that is intended was not observed.
conclusion.confirmed: Browsers and proxies are told not to cache pages. Whether that is right depends on deployment context this analysis cannot see.
conclusion.not_observed: The exported configuration does not set this value to 0.
conclusion.unknown: The exported value could not be established.

finding.evidence_explanation: system.performance:cache.page.max_age was observed as 0 in the exported configuration.
finding.human_title: Browser and proxy caching is switched off in exported configuration
limitations: This is exported configuration, not the runtime effective value.
No runtime performance was measured; this is a configuration observation only.

remediation.guidance: Review whether a non-zero browser and proxy cache maximum age is appropriate for this deployment. If a reverse caching proxy or CDN fronts the site, the documentation notes that disabling page caching there can be deliberate.

review.authority: reviewed against the pinned Internal Page Cache documentation snapshot

scope.notes: The Internal Page Cache module and this setting exist in Drupal 8 and later.
